title: Tighten the remaining engine input guards
description: Follow-up from TASK-1.21 (doc-29) spec and reviews: a few engine entry points still throw native TypeErrors or echo input of any length. Nothing untrusted reaches them today, but saved sessions and replay-code input will.

nodes.title: Tighten the remaining engine input guards
Bootstrap the strict TypeScript project with one-command checks
Rank showdown hands by real poker hand rankings
Deal every hand from a seeded shuffle with a replay code
Play a complete fixed-limit hand from blinds to showdown
Run every check in GitHub Actions on each push and pull request
Harden engine input validation found in review

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given parseCards or evaluate receives a non-array or non-string input, When called, Then it throws RangeError with a message that echoes no input
Given createHand receives a null config or non-array seats, When called, Then it throws RangeError('Invalid hand config') instead of TypeError

Given an invalid seat, button or replay code longer than 10 characters, When the error is built, Then 'Invalid seat', 'Button must be a dealt-in seat' and 'Invalid replay code' echo at most 10 characters plus '...', and TASK-1.3's locked messages for short inputs stay byte-identical

implementationNotes: From TASK-1.31 security review (doc-35): restored sessions (TASK-3.10) are the real source of a non-array seats / null config reaching createHand; AC#2 here owns the RangeError('Invalid hand config') guard.
